open_points.subject: StaffProjectAssignment creation status
open_points.text: The lifecycle is `active → revoked`, but the assignment creation text never states whether a newly created assignment starts active or whether its status may be selected at creation.
open_points.question: What status does `assign_staff_project` give a new StaffProjectAssignment?
options: Every new assignment is created active.
The administrator may create it active or revoked.
A new assignment is initially inactive or otherwise non-authorizing until another action activates it.
open_points.default_guess: Every new assignment is created active.

witness.initial: An active operator has no assignment to an active Registry project.
events: An administrator assigns the operator to the project.
The operator immediately attempts a project read.
outcomes: The assignment was created active, so the authorization check admits the read.
The assignment was not yet active, so the authorization check refuses the read or requires another activation action.

open_points.subject: Direct reading of staff assignments
open_points.text: The text says assignments are created or modified by administrators and consulted for operator authorization, but it does not say whether any product action can get or list assignment records, or whether an operator may read their own scope.
open_points.question: Besides internal authorization checks, which product actions may read StaffProjectAssignment records and who may invoke them?
options: Administrators can list or get assignments; operators cannot.
Administrators can list assignments and operators can read their own assignments.
There is no direct assignment read action; records are read only by authorization and by create/revoke workflows.
open_points.default_guess: Administrators can list assignments; operators have no direct assignment read action.

witness.initial: An active assignment already exists for an operator and project.
events: A different administrator needs to inspect the operator's current project scope.
outcomes: An administrative read/list action returns the assignment and its status.
No direct read exists, so the administrator can only attempt create/revoke operations or infer scope indirectly.

open_points.subject: ServicePrincipal creation status
open_points.text: `status: PrincipalStatus (active | disabled)` and lifecycle `active ↔ disabled` are defined, but `create_service_principal` does not state the initial status or whether creation accepts a status choice.
open_points.question: What status does a newly created ServicePrincipal have?
options: Every new principal is active.
Every new principal is disabled until explicitly enabled.
The administrator chooses active or disabled during creation.

witness.initial: No service principal exists for a producer.
events: An administrator creates a service principal.
An administrator issues it a credential.
The producer authenticates and attempts an import for an allowed active project.
outcomes: The principal was created active, so the import can proceed.
The principal was created disabled, so authentication or authorization refuses the import until an enable action occurs.

open_points.subject: ServicePrincipal name uniqueness
open_points.text: The model defines `name: str` as a human-readable source name but gives no uniqueness, normalization, or duplicate-name rule.
open_points.question: May two ServicePrincipal records have the same name?
options: Names are non-unique labels; identity is only `service_principal_id`.
Names are globally unique.
Names are unique within `source_type`.
open_points.default_guess: Names are non-unique labels; identity is only `service_principal_id`.

witness.initial: An active service principal named `PresuPro` already exists.
events: An administrator creates another principal with the name `PresuPro`.
outcomes: Creation succeeds and two distinct principal IDs share the same display name.
Creation is refused because the name is unique globally or within the source type.

open_points.subject: Initial ServiceCredential creation
open_points.text: State 0 says a ServicePrincipal has “one or more independently revocable credentials,” while M13 says an administrator creates the principal and M14 separately says credentials are created by an administrator; no text says whether principal creation also issues the first credential.
open_points.question: Does creating a ServicePrincipal atomically create and return its first ServiceCredential, or can the principal exist with no credential until a separate issue action?
options: Principal creation atomically issues the first credential and returns its secret once.
Principal creation creates only the principal; a separate action issues the first credential.
Principal creation optionally issues a credential according to request input.
open_points.default_guess: Principal creation creates only the principal, followed by a separate credential-issue action.

witness.initial: No principal or credential exists for a new integration.
events: An administrator creates the service principal.
The administrator does not perform any further action.
outcomes: A principal and its first credential exist, and the creation response contained the one-time secret.
Only the principal exists and it cannot authenticate until a separate credential is issued.

open_points.subject: Direct reading of service principals
open_points.text: `ServicePrincipalView` is defined and administrators “manage service principals,” but the text does not state whether principals can be listed or fetched, or whether the view is returned only by create/status-change actions.
open_points.question: Which product actions directly read ServicePrincipal records?
options: Administrators can list and get service principals.
Administrators can list but not fetch an individual principal.
There is no direct read action; ServicePrincipalView appears only in mutation responses.
open_points.default_guess: Administrators can list and get service principals.

witness.initial: A service principal exists, but its identifier is not available to the current administrator.
events: The administrator attempts to inspect existing integrations before issuing or revoking a credential.
outcomes: A principal list or lookup returns its ID, status, source type, and scope mode.
No direct read exists, so the administrator cannot discover it through the product API.

open_points.subject: When imported section linking creates plans and PortalSections
open_points.text: The section-linking text says the operation must build the imported version, plans and new sections “before activation so that operators can re-allocate to those sections,” while `BudgetActivationResult` says it is produced after “activation, section linking, previous-version deactivation, and audit commit atomically.”
open_points.question: Does section linking and creation of imported plans/new PortalSections happen before activation in a separate version-building action, or atomically inside activation?
options: A pre-activation action builds the inactive imported version, plans, and sections; activation later only validates resolution and switches versions.
Activation atomically performs section linking, creates plans and sections, deactivates the old version, and activates the new one.
A pre-activation action creates provisional links, but activation recreates or finalizes them atomically.
open_points.default_guess: A pre-activation action builds the inactive imported version, plans, and sections; activation later switches versions after unresolved allocations are cleared.

witness.initial: A project has an active manual version, an expense allocated to a manual section, and an accepted snapshot containing a new unmatched source section.
events: A staff member selects the snapshot as the candidate imported version.
The staff member needs to re-allocate the expense to the new imported section.
outcomes: The inactive imported version and its new PortalSection already exist, so the staff member can re-allocate first and then activate.
The new PortalSection is created only inside activation, but activation is refused while the old allocation is unresolved, leaving no pre-activation target to which the staff member can re-allocate.
witness.observer: The staff member performing budget transition
